# Results — Study 893 (Vol-Target 60/40)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — a **volatility
thermostat** on the balanced 60/40 book (scale total exposure by inverse realized portfolio vol to
a constant target) improves the excess-of-cash Sharpe and cuts drawdown vs the static 60/40, net of
the extra turnover. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. Data as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current
month is dropped). Fingerprint `a874e54fa109` (SPY/IEF/AGG/BIL total-return prices).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes (`auto_adjust=True`, **total return**): SPY (stocks), IEF (7–10y Tsy), AGG (agg bonds, robustness leg), **BIL** (1–3m T-bills, the cash proxy), **2007-05-31 → 2026-06-30**, 4,801 return rows |
| Static book | fixed **60% SPY / 40% IEF**, rebalanced on the first trading day of each calendar year (Study 97's Real/Investable default) |
| Thermostat | `w_t = σ_target / σ̂_{t−1}`, clipped to `[0, 2.0]`; `σ̂` = trailing **21-day realized portfolio vol** of the static blend, **lagged one day** (zero look-ahead); hold `w_t` of the blend, park `(1 − w_t)` in cash |
| Fair race | `σ_target` set to the static blend's own realized vol (**10.67%/yr**) so the two books run the **same average risk** and only *re-time* it; both arms measured **excess-of-cash** (minus BIL) |
| Costs | one-way bps × overlay `\|Δw\|` per day **+** 50 bps/yr borrow on the levered fraction `max(w−1, 0)`; the static baseline pays the same one-way bps on its annual rebalance |
| Statistics | leverage-clean **Moreira–Muir spanning alpha** (managed-on-static OLS, HAC *t* on the intercept); a circular block-bootstrap CI on the excess-**Sharpe difference**; a raw HAC *t* on the return difference (contaminated — see below); a two-era cut; a 30-seed synthetic control |

**Short history — named on the Signal axis.** BIL (the cash leg) lists **2007-05-30**, which bounds
the joint window to ~19 years — one that *starts inside the GFC*. That is a young-ETF, single-cycle
sample: the numbers below are one 19-year draw, not a law.

**Why not just a *t* on the return difference?** Because `E[1/σ̂] > 1/E[σ̂]` (Jensen), the thermostat
runs average exposure slightly **above 1**, so a plain *t* on the daily return difference picks up
that *level tilt* rather than the re-timing skill — and it fires even on a flat-vol null. The
**leverage-invariant** reads are the *spanning alpha* and the *Sharpe-difference* CI, and those
lead the verdict.

## The race — static 60/40 vs vol-targeted 60/40 (matched average risk, gross)

| book | excess Sharpe | CAGR | vol | max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| static 60/40 | **0.682** | 8.43% | 10.68% | **−29.6%** |
| vol-targeted 60/40 | **0.808** | 10.33% | 11.26% | **−24.2%** |

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| excess-vs-excess Sharpe gain | **+0.126** |
| Moreira–Muir spanning alpha (leverage-clean) | **+2.31%/yr**, HAC ***t* = +1.92** (β = 0.931) |
| raw return-diff HAC *t* (level-contaminated) | +1.63 |
| avg leverage / levered days / capped days | 1.36× / 74% / 18% |
| overlay turnover | 9.4×/yr |

The thermostat's point estimates all favour it — Sharpe **0.682 → 0.808**, drawdown **−29.6% →
−24.2%** — but the risk-adjusted *improvement* sits **just under the bar**: the leverage-clean
spanning-alpha *t* is **1.92 (< 2)**.

## Bootstrap — circular block CI on the excess Sharpe difference (2,000 resamples)

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| Sharpe gain | **+0.126** |
| 95% CI | **[−0.086, +0.323]** |
| P(vol-target wins) | 87.8% |

**The CI straddles zero** (P(gain < 0) ≈ 12%). The point estimate is a clean positive; the
uncertainty band is not.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2015-01-01)

| era | n | Sharpe gain | spanning alpha *t* | maxDD static → vt |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2007-05 → 2014-12 | 1,891 | **+0.217** | +1.86 | −29.6% → −25.6% |
| 2015-01 → 2026-06 | 2,868 | **+0.058** | +0.93 | −21.4% → −16.4% |

The Sharpe edge is **concentrated in the GFC-containing first half and fades to +0.06** post-2015
(*t* 1.86 → 0.93). **The drawdown reduction, by contrast, holds in *both* eras** (~4–5 pts) — the
robust half of the story.

## Window robustness — no magic point (gross, matched risk)

| vol window | Sharpe gain | spanning alpha *t* | overlay turnover | maxDD (vt) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21-day | +0.126 | +1.92 | 9.4×/yr | −24.2% |
| 42-day | +0.088 | +1.59 | 5.2×/yr | −24.6% |
| 63-day | +0.054 | +1.22 | 3.6×/yr | −23.6% |

The Sharpe gain **shrinks as the window lengthens** (the extra edge lives in the fast, turnover-hungry
21-day forecast); the drawdown reduction is window-insensitive.

## Costed — the tradability test

One-way bps on overlay turnover **+ 50 bps/yr borrow** on the levered fraction (the static baseline
pays the same one-way bps on its annual rebalance):

| one-way cost | static Sharpe | vt Sharpe | Sharpe gain | maxDD (vt) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bp | 0.682 | 0.789 | **+0.107** | −24.3% |
| 1 bp | 0.682 | 0.781 | **+0.098** | −24.4% |
| 2 bp | 0.682 | 0.772 | **+0.090** | −24.5% |
| 5 bp | 0.682 | 0.747 | **+0.065** | −24.8% |
| 10 bp | 0.682 | 0.705 | **+0.023** | −25.3% |

The **drawdown reduction survives every realistic cost** (−24% to −25% throughout, on the two most
liquid ETFs on earth — capacity is not the constraint). The thin **Sharpe** gain is eaten from +0.11
to +0.02 by 10 bp + borrow: real but fragile.

## Crash-year drawdown — the robust half (calendar-year total return)

| year | static 60/40 | vol-targeted 60/40 |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2008 | −14.9% | **−13.2%** |
| 2022 | −17.0% | **−14.1%** |

Both of the balanced book's worst years were shallower under the thermostat — the mechanical
risk-control benefit, needing no significance test.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded 60/40 world: a sticky Markov chain scales the **common** shock size of both
assets (so *portfolio* vol clusters) around a **regime-independent** drift. `sigma_lo == sigma_hi` is
the flat-vol null. No network.

| world | spanning alpha *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (flat vol), **30 seeds** | mean **+0.20**, **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/30** (≈ the 5% false-positive rate) |
| planted (clustered), **30 seeds** | mean **+3.09**, **t ≥ 2 in 23/30** |

The detector recovers a *planted* vol-targeting edge and stays quiet on the null — so the *real-tape*
sub-significance is a genuine property of the 60/40 tape, not a broken engine.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Every point estimate favours the thermostat (excess Sharpe **0.682 → 0.808**,
  spanning alpha **+2.31%/yr**, drawdown **−29.6% → −24.2%**), and the **drawdown/risk-control
  benefit is real and robust** (holds in both eras and every crash year, needs no *t*). But the
  risk-adjusted **improvement** does not clear the desk's bar: the leverage-clean spanning-alpha HAC
  ***t* = 1.92 (< 2)**, the bootstrap Sharpe-difference **CI [−0.086, +0.323] straddles zero**
  (P(gain < 0) ≈ 12%), the edge **fades across eras** (*t* 1.86 → 0.93; gain +0.22 → +0.06 post-2015)
  and **thins as the vol window lengthens**. A single-cycle, GFC-anchored, ~19-year BIL-bounded
  window. The Sharpe lift is directionally there but sub-significant; the honest stamp is Weak.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The *bankable* part — the drawdown reduction — survives every realistic
  cost on the two most liquid ETFs alive (turnover ~9×/yr, capacity ~unbounded). But the **Sharpe
  edge itself is thin, decaying, and leverage-financed** (avg 1.36×, levered 74% of days, capped 18%),
  and a 50 bp borrow + a few bp turnover eats it from +0.11 to +0.02 by 10 bp. A real-but-thin,
  decaying, leverage-dependent overlay is **Fragile**, not Investable: you run it for the shallower
  drawdown, not for a certified Sharpe pickup.
